evidence_quotes.name_asked_and_used: Rep says 'Hi Jake!' after customer introduces himself and uses the name multiple times throughout
evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'This would only take within the next ten to fifteen minutes of your time so I can build an accurate code. Would that be okay with you?' — time-boxed but promise of dependable quote is absent; customer gives a yes but it's somewhat unclear due to audio quality
evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Never asked. No version of the two-concerns framing about on-time arrival or damage appears anywhere in the call
evidence_quotes.promises_delivered: No On-Time Guarantee or No Worries Damage Coverage mentioned at any point
evidence_quotes.concern_led_opening: Missing. Rep jumps directly into logistics ('is the elevator reserved') without asking 'What items in this move are you most concerned about?'
evidence_quotes.logistics_gathered: Addresses obtained (600 Guadalupe to 1800 South Lamar), property type (one bedroom apartment), floor/elevator situation, walking distance clarified, special items asked about (safe, piano, equipment) — but customer states only moving one mattress, so most detail buckets don't apply
evidence_quotes.packing_and_box_count: Packing question about mattress wrapping comes up late and organically ('The movers when we bring like, so anything else, maybe they wrap the mattress') but never formally asked; no box count question since move is minimal
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep mentions minimum of 2.5 hours at $520 and that billing goes to 15-minute increments ('it will always be prorated to fifteen minute increments') — this covers fee transparency and not-a-guess elements, but no pricing contrast (competitors' hourly vs all-inclusive), no 'no need to take notes' line, and no clear three-part framing
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gives '$520 minimum' and personalizes slightly by explaining it applies even though customer is moving one item, but no typical range for a home this size is offered and no real pause held after the number
evidence_quotes.value_days: Never addressed. No mention of cheaper days, date flexibility, or Value Days framework
evidence_quotes.prep_and_temperature_check: Not present. No Save Your Ass framing about prep being the biggest factor, no 'How do you feel about that?' temperature check
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Call moves straight to booking confirmation without a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' check
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_and_ask: Rep says 'there's no deposit required, no recent securing your spot' and then 'Would you like me to lock that in for you?' — rate lock and no deposit clearly stated before the ask, and the ask is plain and direct without a built-in out
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Date (October 22nd, later adjusted to 2:00 PM window), time window (1:00 PM to 2:00 PM per customer preference, later 2:00 PM with 1:00–3:00 PM window), addresses confirmed, and confirmation email promised; crew size and detailed notes about customer concerns are missing

top_strength: The rep successfully booked the move and confirmed the key details (date, time window, addresses) with clear, direct language, and correctly laid out no-deposit rate-locking before asking for the business.
coaching_note: This call skipped the two foundational steps of Einstein's process: never asked the two-concerns question (step 2) or delivered the two key promises about on-time guarantee and damage protection (step 3), which means the customer left with no differentiation from competitors and no answer to their unstated concerns about reliability.
